headline: Highest risk is medium: shared data-engineering workflows can create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error paths, but no direct shared channel or sensitive-data handling is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can call REST/GRPC APIs and Superset exposes a Superset API, so a manual or API-mediated content bridge is plausible. However, neither profile documents a shared filesystem, clipboard, or direct ingestion of the other’s outputs, so the injection path is not default and remains limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies Argo-generated text into Superset prompts or dashboards, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared API or message bridge is added between the two, attacker-controlled content can traverse it.
mitigations: Require explicit human review before copying outputs between systems.
Strip instructions from any text passed from Argo to Superset.
Use separate service accounts and API gateways for each system.
Log and diff all cross-system payloads before execution.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo touches artifacts and parameters, while Superset’s profile shows no data classes touched. Both have allowlisted egress, but there is no documented shared workspace or secret handling, so leakage is possible only through operator-managed transfers rather than a default pairwise channel.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or bucket, artifacts may be exposed across tools.
IF sensitive parameters are copied from Argo into Superset inputs, they can appear in Superset outputs or logs.
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces and buckets for each tool.
Avoid placing secrets in workflow parameters.
Review Superset dashboards for accidental display of raw inputs.
Rotate any credentials copied into shared locations.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have allowlisted network egress and API-call surfaces, but neither profile shows filesystem write, git mutation, or overlapping OAuth scopes. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the remaining risk is limited to coordinated API usage or operator confusion.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external API resource, they can overwrite each other’s changes.
IF an orchestrator later adds shared mutable state, conflicts may emerge.
mitigations: Assign distinct API credentials per system.
Use optimistic locking on any shared resource.
Separate write targets by environment or namespace.
Monitor for conflicting updates in shared endpoints.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo can produce workflow artifacts and parameters that Superset may ingest for analytics or visualization. Because neither profile documents a verification step or provenance tracking, B could treat A’s outputs as authoritative and propagate errors into downstream reports, even though no direct action-taking authority is shown.
conditions: IF Superset dashboards are built directly from Argo outputs without validation, incorrect values can cascade.
IF operators use Superset results to make decisions, the error propagates beyond the original workflow.
mitigations: Add schema validation before importing Argo outputs.
Mark imported fields as untrusted in Superset.
Require a second review for dashboards built from workflow artifacts.
Display source provenance on every imported metric.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented in either profile. Argo touches artifacts and parameters, but Superset lists no sensitive data classes or compliance constraints, so there is no evidenced compliance pathway to score.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated data through either agent, a separate compliance review is required.
IF retention or residency policies are configured differently later, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both systems.
Confirm retention settings before production use.
Keep regulated datasets out of unreviewed workflows.
